title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Design Specs, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes (2028-04-15)
author: Ava Patel
summary: This document consolidates the product overview, PRD-level requirements, design specifications, roadmap & themes, pricing and packaging notes, and the release notes for the Unified Inference product family as of the 2028-04-15 release. It is intended for PMs, engineering, sales, and support teams responsible for product planning, customer communications, and rollout execution.
product_overview:
## Product overview

Unified Inference is Redwood's core product family that offers a single API and control plane to run LLM inference across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The product objective is to deliver predictable latency, transparent unit economics, and operational controls (routing, caching, batching, and rollouts) so engineering teams can ship LLM features with minimal infra overhead. Key capabilities: 

- Single REST/SDK surface for text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking.
- Smart routing and model variant fallback to meet latency/cost SLOs.
- Integrated observability (token-level cost, per-model latency, error traces).
- Configurable autoscaling, dedicated GPU pools, and private VPC deployments.

This document describes the 2028-04-15 release (Unified Inference v4.2) and the product priorities and subsequent roadmap themes through Q4 2028.
prd_requirements:
## PRD: High-level requirements (v4.2 release)

Goals:
1) Improve tail latency by 20% for 99th percentile across standard generation workloads.
2) Reduce per-token serving cost by 12% for enterprise text generation use cases via improved batching and caching heuristics.
3) Launch simplified pricing tiers and packaging for self-serve and Dedicated customers.
4) Provide a clear upgrade path and compatibility guarantees for Private deployments.

Success metrics:
- 99th percentile p95/p99 latency against baseline (measurements in benchmarking suite).
- Mean per-token cost (USD) for standard workloads.
- NPS change among top 50 customers after rollout.
- Adoption: 30% of active customers adopt the new pricing tier within 90 days.

Functional requirements (selected):
- FR-01: Runtime must support per-request policy-based routing (latency-first, cost-first, region-first).
- FR-02: Automatic KV/prefix caching with adaptive TTLs configurable per-route.
- FR-03: Continuous batching that respects latency SLOs and can be tuned per-customer.
- FR-04: Model catalog metadata API with quantization and perf profile flags.
- FR-05: Pricing API & billing metadata (so customers can query estimated per-request cost before execution).

Non-functional requirements:
- NFR-01: Platform SLO: 99.95% availability for hosted inference endpoints.
- NFR-02: Security: AES-256 encryption in transit and at rest; integration with customer KMS for Private deployments.
- NFR-03: Compliance: preserve audit logs for 365 days (enterprise customers).

Backward compatibility and migration:
- Private deployments v3.x must be able to opt into v4.2 features through configuration flags. Migration docs and an automated preflight checker are required (see rollout_and_migration).
design_spec:
## Design spec (selected highlights)

1) Runtime Kernel & Scheduling
- Continuous batching engine: adaptive micro-batching that groups tokens across concurrent requests while respecting per-request deadline metadata.
- Kernel selector: runtime selects between FP16/INT8 kernels based on model profile and customer preferences; fallback to FP32 for unquantized models.
- KV cache sharding: cache is sharded per model-version + tenant with LRU eviction; metadata exposes hit-rate per-route.

2) Smart Routing & Fallbacks
- Policy engine supports three primary routing policies: latency_first, cost_first, and geo_affinity. Each policy is evaluated at request admission with a scoring function that includes current GPU queue length, observed mean latency for the route, and estimated token cost.
- When capacity constraints or kernel incompatibilities occur, requests are automatically downgraded to compatible variants (e.g., smaller model family or lower quantization) following a priority table defined per tenant.

3) Observability & Debugging
- Token-level cost attribution: trace ID emits per-token compute/IO cost estimates that feed into the Console billing view.
- Per-route dashboards: P95/P99 latency, batch-size distribution, cache hit-rate, and model-regression alerts tied to evaluation prompt sets.

4) Configuration schema (sample)
- route_config: {\"route_id\": \"string\", \"policy\": \"latency_first|cost_first|geo_affinity\", \"cache\": {\"enabled\": true, \"ttl_ms\": 30000}, \"batch\": {\"max_window_ms\": 20, \"max_tokens\": 2048}}

(Implementation note: the real system stores this as YAML/JSON in the Control Plane DB; above is a concise reference for engineers.)
roadmap_and_themes:
## Roadmap & themes (Q2-Q4 2028)

Themes by quarter:
- Q2 2028 (current): Tail latency reduction; simplified pricing tiers; release v4.2.
- Q3 2028: Advanced quality controls (prompt-guard rails, automatic eval-based rollbacks); Dedicated autoscaling improvements.
- Q4 2028: Private deployment automation (one-click preflight + airgap-safe package); multi-region failover & cross-region replication.

Planned milestones:
1. 2028-04-15: v4.2 GA (tail latency optimizations, new pricing tiers, new routing policies).
2. 2028-06-30: v4.3 Beta (eval-driven rollback automation, per-route quality monitoring).
3. 2028-09-15: v5.0 (private deployment automation, major control plane upgrade).

Cross-cutting initiatives:
- Cost Controls: tie-model suggestions to customer usage patterns (Redwood Optimize integration).
- Reliability: expand canary and A/B rollout tooling in Console; automatic fallback policy improvements.

Dependencies and risks:
- Kernel vendor updates: kernel upgrades on some platforms may be gated by upstream driver changes.
- Fleet capacity: Dedicated and burst capacity must be provisioned ahead of Q4 private rollouts.
- Customer migration effort: Private customers may require on-prem preflight checks and extended support windows.
pricing_and_packaging:
## Pricing & packaging notes (summary)

Objectives:
- Simplify self-serve and enterprise pricing to improve conversion.
- Make cost tradeoffs explicit (latency vs. cost) and expose tooling to customers to control them.

Tiers (effective 2028-04-15):
- Developer (self-serve): pay-as-you-go, standard throughput, 30-day retention for logs, web support.
- Team: committed monthly credits, lower per-token price, basic SLA (99.9%), phone/email support.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools, negotiated commit, SLA 99.95%, longer log retention (90 days), access to autoscaling policies.
- Private Enterprise: deployment license + support (annual), deployment automation package, compliance add-ons (SOC2+, HIPAA), custom SLAs.

Pricing mechanics highlights:
- Per-token pricing disaggregated by model-family (small/medium/large) and compute class (CPU/GPU-A100/GPU-H100).
- Billing API: customers can request an estimated cost per request before execution.
- Discounting: committed usage discounts applied after threshold usage; Dedicated pricing negotiated as monthly/annual commit.

Notes for sales and enablement:
- Provide a migration worksheet mapping existing commitments to new tiers and estimated monthly savings using historical usage.
- Call out sensitive customers (HIPAA, FedRAMP) that require Private packaging and longer procurement cycles.
release_notes:
## Release notes: Unified Inference v4.2 (GA: 2028-04-15)

Overview:
v4.2 focuses on tail-latency reduction, cost improvements from smarter batching/caching, expanded routing policies, and the rollout of the new simplified pricing tiers. This release is GA for Hosted and Dedicated customers; Private customers may opt in after preflight checks.

Major features:
- Tail latency optimizations: adaptive micro-batching and deadline-aware scheduling reduced p99 by 18-25% in internal benchmarks (depending on workload).
- Adaptive KV/prefix caching: improved cache hit rates for common prompt prefixes; configurable TTL per-route.
- Routing policy engine: new cost_first and geo_affinity policies; scoring function and fallbacks added.
- Pricing & Billing API: estimate_cost endpoint added to the public API (see API examples in eng-developer-experience).
- Console updates: per-route cost breakdowns and a new rollout UI for canary/A-B rollouts.

Bug fixes & performance improvements:
- Fixed an INT8 decoding stall under certain model sharding patterns.
- Reduced control-plane latency for route updates (average update applied within 2s).

Known issues:
1) Private installs on older GPU drivers may see degraded INT8 performance. Workaround: pin kernel to FP16 until driver is upgraded.
2) Extremely high concurrency ( > 100k concurrent connections per region) can cause longer scheduling decision times; mitigation: shard traffic across routes and enable geo_affinity routing.

Deprecations:
- Legacy /v1/batch endpoint is deprecated; customers should migrate to the /v2/generate endpoint by 2028-07-01.
rollout_and_migration:
## Rollout plan & migration notes

Staged rollout (Hosted & Dedicated):
1) Canary (2028-04-15 to 2028-04-22): 5% of traffic on internal blue cluster; monitor p95/p99, cache hit-rate, and error budget.
2) Gradual ramp (2028-04-23 to 2028-05-07): increase to 50% with automated rollback thresholds (p99 increase > 10% or error rate > 0.5%).
3) Full rollout (2028-05-08): 100% traffic.

Private migrations:
- Provide preflight tool (CLI) that validates kernel/driver, network egress rules, KMS access, and disk layout.
- Private customers required to schedule migration windows; recommended rollback snapshot and fallback routes defined in the preflight report.

Customer communication checklist:
- Customer-facing release notes (support) and targeted emails to top 50 customers.
- Update public API docs and SDKs; deprecation notices for /v1/batch.
- Sales enablement: migration sheet and pricing comparison calculator.

Rollback & incident runbook highlights:
1) If p99 latency regression detected above threshold, automatically shift traffic to previous model-variant via routing policy.
2) If control-plane regressions occur, enable hot-failover to read-only mode and notify SRE oncall.

Testing & verification:
- Regression test suite (eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite) must pass with no more than 2% regression in mean latency across sample workloads before an environment can proceed from canary to ramp.
